summary.text: Blood is a specialized connective tissue and body fluid that delivers nutrients and oxygen to the cells and carries metabolic waste products away from them.
It is made of blood cells suspended in plasma, and the cells are mainly red blood cells, white blood cells and, in mammals, platelets.
The pumping action of the heart circulates blood around the body through the blood vessels.

facts.label: Plasma share
facts.value: 55% of blood fluid, and mostly water

facts.label: Colour
facts.value: Bright red when oxygenated, dark red when not

items.prompt: After a paper cut, bleeding stops as the blood clots. Which blood component takes part in that clotting?
items.explain: Platelets are important in the clotting of blood.

items.prompt: What do red blood cells hold that lets them carry oxygen around the body?
items.explain: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, which reversibly binds oxygen and increases its solubility, facilitating transport.

items.prompt: A sample of blood looks dark red. What does that say about its hemoglobin?
items.explain: Blood is bright red when its hemoglobin is oxygenated and dark red when it is deoxygenated.

items.prompt: Germs enter a wound. Which blood cells help the body resist infections and parasites?
items.explain: White blood cells (leukocytes) help resist infections and parasites and are part of the immune system.

items.prompt: A lab removes the clotting proteins from a sample of plasma. What is the leftover fluid called?
items.explain: Serum refers to plasma from which the clotting proteins have been removed.

items.prompt: A vet studies a lizard's blood. Which cells do the clotting job that platelets do in humans?

options.label: Flattened, ovoid red cells that lack nuclei
Platelets, exactly as they work in humans
White cells that build a mesh of fibrin

items.explain: Platelets are unique to mammals; in other vertebrates, small nucleated spindle cells called thrombocytes handle clotting instead.
